transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ava Thompson (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Liu Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (Athena PM), Carlos Vega (Athena Eng Lead), Priya Menon (Athena DS), Owen Li (Athena Security)

Summary (auto): Kickoff for Athena POC to validate quality guardrails for document-insight feature. Focus on golden prompts, regression sets, hallucination detection, scoring, and a practical timeline for a 4-week pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into objectives.
[00:10] Maya (Athena PM): Hi all, Maya here. We're excited — we've been wanting to lock down how to measure hallucinations for our docs feature.
[00:16] Carlos (Athena): Carlos — I'll be owning the engineering side, curious about throughput and rollout risk.
[00:20] Ava: Awesome. Samir and Liu from our SE team will handle the bench and the deeper evals. Samir, you wanna frame the plan?
[00:27] Samir (Redwood SE): Yeah quick high level. We're proposing a four week POC. Week one is sample ingestion + smoke benchmarks on hosted Redwood models. Week two build golden prompt set and initial regression suite. Week three run full load and refine scoring. Week four acceptance and handoff, plus a run of fallback tests for dedicated/private if needed.
[00:46] Priya (Athena DS): Can you define "golden prompts" for the doc-insight flow? We have extraction plus classification tasks.
[00:52] Liu (Redwood SE): Sure, golden prompts are a curated set of prompts and input-output pairs that define expected behavior. For extraction tasks we want canonical examples — edge cases, noisy OCR, nested entities, truncated context. We'll use them both for absolute quality checks and regression to catch regressions after tuning/quant.
[01:13] Maya: Sounds good. Our main success criteria are precision on key entities > 92% and hallucination rate under 3% on the golden set. Latency target is 95th perc < 800ms for single-doc sync calls; throughput target 40 reqs/s for peak. Are those realistic?
[01:33] Samir: Precision 92% is achievable depending on the model family and prompt engineering. Hallucination under 3% is aggressive but doable; need to define how you measure hallucination (free-text hallucination vs fabricated facts in structured outputs). We typically use a binary hallucination flag at the item level plus severity scores.
[01:49] Carlos: For throughput, if we host on Redwood dedicated, can we reserve capacity? We don't want noisy neighbor issues.
[01:55] Ava: Yes dedicated pools are available. For POC we'll start hosted to iterate quickly, then we can simulate dedicated capacity in bench to get the latency/throughput numbers.
[02:04] Owen (Athena Sec): Quick pause on data — we can't send PHI to hosted unless encrypted and governed. We'll need VPC or on-prem option for later stages. For the POC we can obfuscate or use synthetic corpora; we'll confirm with legal.
[02:14] Ava: Understood — plan B is to mask or synth the corpus. For the smoke benchmark we can run on a masked subset.
[02:19] Priya: On the regression tests — what size do you recommend? We have an existing test harness but not a golden set.
[02:26] Samir: Typical approach: 200-500 golden prompts for coverage of critical flows + 2-5k regression cases drawn from live logs for distributional checks. For hallucination detection we add 300 adversarial prompts that historically trigger fabrication.
[02:39] Maya: We can provide the 2-5k from logs but need to strip PII. Priya and I will scope that.
[02:44] Carlos: How will you score outputs? Are we doing automated scoring or human-in-the-loop?
[02:49] Liu: Hybrid. We'll run automatic checks for format/required fields and entity overlap metrics (precision/recall/F1). For semantic hallucination we'll seed a human review sample — say 10% of golden failures — to label severity. We'll report a composite quality score: Weighted F1 (70%) + hallucination penalty (20%) + format/structure pass rate (10%). We can tune weights to your risk profile.
[03:12] Priya: That weighting makes sense, but can we see an example scorecard?
[03:16] Samir: Yes — we'll attach a sample spreadsheet with per-prompt metrics: tokens, latency, top-1 match, F1, hallucination flag, severity, owner notes.
[03:27] Maya: For golden prompts, what formats do you accept? JSON lines with input/output?
[03:31] Ava: JSONL with fields: id, prompt_input, expected_output, category, difficulty, notes. We'll send a template.
[03:39] Owen: Security again — audit logs and KMS support? For later adoption we need SSE+K, KMS integration, and retention policies. Also SAML SSO for the console.
[03:49] Ava: All supported on Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports audit logs and encryption-at-rest; KMS and SSO available for enterprise tier/private. We'll include a security checklist doc.
[03:58] Carlos: Ok. Back to benchmarks — how do you handle quantized models? We care about cost so quantization is interesting but worried about accuracy regression.
[04:06] Samir: We'll benchmark float32 baseline, then int8/int4 variants where supported. Part of the POC is a regression suite that runs across variants and flags regression exceeding your thresholds (e.g., F1 drop > 2 points). We also measure per-token cost and latency delta.
[04:22] Maya: Timeline — I count four weeks. Can you propose specific milestones?
[04:26] Samir: Week 0 (this week): kickoff, templates, corpus ask. Week 1: ingestion + smoke run + baseline metrics. Week 2: build golden prompts + regression design. Week 3: full benchmarks across variants, human review sampling. Week 4: acceptance, handoff, and runbook. We can compress if you provide data faster.
[04:44] Priya: For smoke run, what's a minimal corpus?
[04:47] Liu: 200-500 documents for a small smoke; 2k+ for meaningful distributional coverage. For latency we can use synthetic traffic to reach 40 req/s.
[04:56] Carlos: How will we measure hallucination programmatically? Any standard heuristics?
[05:00] Samir: Several heuristics: entity hallucination (entities present but not supported by context), contradiction detection (cross-check answers vs source text), knowledge cutoff hits (model invents facts beyond provided doc). We also use embedding-similarity to the source to detect unsupported claims. None are perfect — hence the human sampling.
[05:18] Maya: Good, include an example of an embedding-similarity threshold that correlates to hallucination.
[05:22] Samir: Yep will add that to the bench doc.
[05:25] Owen: Privacy note — for embedding similarity we'll keep vector data in your VPC if Private. For hosted tests we'll hash/obfuscate.
[05:31] Ava: Ok next, acceptance criteria recap. Maya can you confirm the targets?
[05:34] Maya: Sure. Targets: precision on priority entities >= 92% (on golden set), overall F1 >= 0.88, hallucination rate <= 3% (item-level), format pass >= 98%, 95th latency <= 800ms on our typical doc sizes. Cost per 1k tokens target TBD after first smoke.
[05:51] Ava: Great. We'll codify those into the acceptance section of the test plan.
[05:56] Carlos: One more — regression cadence. After POC, how do we keep regressions out of prod?
[06:00] Liu: Recommend an automated gate: every model change triggers the regression suite; if weighted quality score drops below acceptance, fail the rollout and flag for manual review. We can integrate with your CI/CD.
[06:10] Priya: Sounds ideal.
[06:12] Maya: Anything on tooling? Do you provide a dashboard?
[06:15] Ava: Redwood Console will show per-prompt breakdowns, token cost, latency histograms, and regression diffs. We'll demo that in the next call.
[06:24] Samir: Also we'll include a benchmark sheet that simulates cost for hosted vs dedicated at your traffic shape, and quantized savings.
[06:31] Maya: Perfect.
[06:33] Owen: Security follow-ups are on me; I'll send constraints.
[06:36] Ava: Thanks — we'll capture that as an action. Any final Qs?
[06:40] Priya: One ask — can you include a short set of adversarial prompts that target hallucination for our domain?
[06:46] Samir: Yes, we'll include ~300 adversarial cases and examples of how they map to severity bins.
[06:52] Ava: Alright, quick recap of next steps: we'll send templates and the bench spreadsheet, Athena will provide corpus and taxonomy, schedule smoke run for 2026-11-06, and Samir will run initial benchmarks.
[07:03] Maya: Thanks everyone. Looking forward.
[07:06] Ava: Thanks, meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcript includes occasional misrecognitions in auto-captioning (e.g., K/V cache transcribed as "K slash V cash"). Human summary to follow.
